t: These ruins and the garden around them are what remains of Christ Church Greyfriars, opposite St Paul's Cathedral. It began as a monastic church in the thirteenth century, and after the Great Fire it was rebuilt by Sir Christopher Wren. Bombing in the Second World War destroyed most of it, apart from the tower, and it was never rebuilt. Several queens and royal women are buried here, including Isabella of France, wife of Edward II, and Margaret of France, second wife of Edward I. So is Thomas Malory, author of Le Morte d'Arthur.
